scenicChapters.title: Sacred Valley Route
scenicChapters.narrative: For 34 km this is Sacred Valley Route, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it. Expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast.

scenicChapters.title: Sacred Valley Route
scenicChapters.narrative: Cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it. The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 4316 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Abra Malaga → Santa Teresa
scenicChapters.narrative: 4316 m come off over 60 km at around 11.2%. The road gives back what the climb took, faster than it took it — brakes early, eyes far ahead. A descent this long asks more of concentration than of pace.

sacred-valley-route.story: A one-way ride of 218 km, Cusco to Santa Teresa - roughly 3 h 01 in the saddle. On the way it passes Pisac, Urubamba, Ollantaytambo and Abra Malaga. The highest point is about 4,300 m. It suits an unhurried touring pace.

scenicChapters.title: Saint Petersburg Imperial Shore
scenicChapters.narrative: Water arrives beside the road and stays for 34 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go — slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did.

scenicChapters.title: A-121 Ladoga and Sortavala
scenicChapters.narrative: For 37 km this is A-121 Ladoga and Sortavala, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it. Expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast.

places-oranienbaumsky-springboard-koltus.story: A 180 km round trip from Petrodvorets - roughly 3 h 17 in the saddle.
